scopeTitle: CREA3 — Conflict Resolution with Equitative Algorithms
scopeTagline: AI-assisted, game-theoretical online dispute resolution for Europe.
scopeIntro1: CREA3 brings AI-driven tools and game-theoretical algorithms to civil dispute resolution. It guides people step by step toward a fair, efficient and tailored outcome, helping them find the information they need along the way.
scopeIntro2: In parallel, it tackles the differences between the national legal systems of the EU Member States so that cross-border disputes can be handled on common ground.
scopeEcgarTitle: European Common Ground of Available Rights (ECGAR)
scopeEcgarText: The mandatory rules of each Member State are set aside and the procedure operates on the remaining “available rights”. The goal is to widen access to Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) and reduce structural barriers to justice.
scopeWp1Body: Links the ECGAR to the game-theoretical model to set precise standards for integrating law and AI.
scopeWp2Body: Machine-learning tools power an assistant that guides practitioners, legal professionals and ordinary users through the whole procedure.
scopeWp3Body: Smart-contract technology, built with a DApp design methodology, certifies the agreement reached between the parties.
scopeVideoNote: A built-in videoconferencing function lets the mediator meet both parties inside the platform (WP3).
scopeAudienceNote: CREA3 improves the existing CREA platform and is released as open source, for a broad range of EU stakeholders.
scopeClosing: Open-source software, distributed for reuse across the European justice community.

faqIntro: Answers to common questions about accounts, running a dispute, and the platform.
faqCat1Q1: How do I create an account?
faqCat1A1: Open “Register”, enter your email and a password, and submit. Registration and identity are handled by our secure sign-in service (Keycloak).
faqCat1Q2: How do I verify my email?
faqCat1A2: After registering you receive a verification email. Open the link it contains to activate your account. Verification is mandatory before you can sign in.
faqCat1Q3: I didn’t receive the verification email — what now?
faqCat1A3: Check your spam folder first. If it still hasn’t arrived after a few minutes, try signing in: the platform will offer to resend the verification message.
faqCat1A4: Your session has expired or you are not signed in. Sign in again; if it persists, sign out fully and sign back in to refresh your session.
faqCat2Q1: How do I start a dispute?
faqCat2A1: From “My disputes”, create a new dispute, give it a title, then define the items in scope and record your baseline valuations.
faqCat2Q2: Who can invite the other parties?
faqCat2A2: Only the dispute creator can invite parties. Any party may invite a mediator. Invitations are sent by email and can be accepted from the notifications area.
faqCat2A3: Goods are the items being divided or negotiated. Preferences are each party’s per-item star ratings, which capture priorities and acceptable ranges.
faqCat2A4: Once parties are ready, a game-theoretic engine combines everyone’s preferences into a balanced, evidence-based proposal that you can review side by side.
faqCat2Q5: What happens if we don’t accept the proposal?
faqCat2A5: Any party may decline. The case can then move to structured mediation, where a mediator coordinates and you can meet over built-in video.
faqCat2A6: Yes. Each dispute can produce a PDF report of the proposal and a CSV audit trail of the actions taken, for your records.
faqCat3Q1: What can the in-dispute assistant do?
faqCat3A1: It explains terms (“What is mediation?”), suggests next steps, and clarifies outputs (“Explain the proposal in simple terms”). It runs locally via Ollama.
faqCat3Q2: Is the assistant the same as the Legal AI page?
faqCat3A2: No. The in-dispute assistant helps you operate the platform. For legal questions, use the dedicated Legal AI Assistant page.
faqCat3A3: Assistant messages are kept in your browser for the current dispute, so you can return to them. They are not shared with other parties.
faqCat4Q1: How do I change my password or email?
faqCat4A1: Open “Account” from the menu. You can update your email and change your password there.
faqCat4Q2: Can I change the interface language?
faqCat4A2: Yes — use the language selector. The interface is available in the consortium’s seven working languages, and switching does not end your session.
faqCat4Q3: How do I delete my data or account?
faqCat4A3: In “Account” you can delete the dispute data you created, or permanently delete your whole account and its related data.
faqCat4A4: Yes. It targets WCAG AA, is fully keyboard-navigable, and offers high-contrast and reduced-motion options in settings.
helpSubtitle: Quick answers and guidance for creating a dispute, setting preferences, and reaching a resolution.
helpA1: A dispute on CREA3 is a structured procedure for resolving a conflict over how to divide goods. The platform guides every party with AI tools and game-theoretical algorithms toward a fair, efficient, tailored resolution.
helpQ2: How do parties express their preferences?
helpA2: Each party rates every good on a 1–5 star scale to show how important it is to them. These ratings, together with each party’s entitlement share, feed the evaluation that produces the proposal.
helpQ3: How do I invite participants to a dispute?
helpA3:
1. Open your dispute and go to the Participants step.

2. Add a participant by email, with their share of entitlement and an optional role (party or mediator).

3. They receive an email invitation and an in-app notification, and can accept from the notifications area.
helpQ4: How do I add goods to a dispute?
helpA4:
1. During setup, open the Goods step.

2. Add each good with a name and estimated value; optionally mark it as indivisible.

3. Submit to include it in the case.
helpQ5: How does CREA3 produce a solution?
helpA5: CREA3 combines the parties’ ratings and entitlement shares and applies AI and game-theoretical algorithms to generate an allocation that aims to satisfy everyone fairly.\n\nParties can accept or decline the proposal. If it is declined, structured mediation — with video-conference scheduling — is available.
helpQ6: What happens once everyone accepts the proposal?
helpA6: When all parties accept, CREA3 finalises the case and generates a downloadable report as certified proof of the resolution, designed for future smart-contract / blockchain certification workflows.
helpQ7: What is the CREA3 European project?
helpA7: CREA3 builds on CREA (2017–19) and CREA2, introducing AI-driven tools that help users resolve disputes through innovative game-theoretical algorithms, a smart conversational interface, smart-contract certification design, and video-conferencing for mediation.\n\nYou can read the full project scope on the Scope page.

landingHeroTitle: Resolve disputes through a transparent, step-by-step negotiation.
landingHeroBody: CREA3 is an EU co-funded platform for resolving cross-border civil and consumer disputes online. Invite the parties, capture each side’s priorities, and generate a transparent, evidence-based settlement proposal — with structured mediation and secure videoconferencing whenever a case needs them.
landingValPartiesBody: Review what’s in dispute, set your priorities, and accept the proposal or move to mediation.
landingValMediatorsBody: See context, preferences, and proposal metrics in a read-only view, and coordinate conferences.
landingValGovernanceBody: Role-based access and auditable steps produce a clean, exportable record of the outcome.
landingFeaturesBody: Everything a cross-border negotiation needs — secure identity, structured steps, and an auditable record — in one open-source platform.
featSecurityBody: Sign-in runs on Keycloak (OpenID Connect) with mandatory email verification and role-based access.
featProposalsBody: A game-theoretic engine turns each party’s priorities into a balanced, explainable settlement proposal.
featAssistantBody: A built-in assistant runs locally via Ollama and answers “what’s next?” at every step of a case.
featLangBody: The interface follows the user, with translations across the consortium’s seven working languages.
featAuditBody: Every action is logged and exportable as a clean PDF report and a CSV audit trail for the file.
featMediationBody: When parties decline a proposal, schedule structured mediation and meet over built-in video.
landingPartnersBody: CREA3 is built by a European network of seven universities, a continental bar federation, and a consumers’ association — working across eight cities in seven countries.
landingReadyBody: Create an account, verify your email, and sign in to start a case.
